messages:
mika: Heads-up — AcmeOne (large fintech) has asked for 40% off for a 6‑month POC. They’ll convert to a 12‑month dedicated commit if latency <100ms p50 and SOC2+SSO are in place. Asking if we can front-load a deeper discount for the POC and then step down to a smaller ongoing discount. Also asking for a migration credit to help offset switchover costs.

jay: Do we have their workload profile? tokens/request, avg response length, concurrency targets? That 5k qps number you mentioned earlier — is that steady or burst? :thinking:

mika: Quick numbers from the RFP: ~1,200 tokens per request (including system + user + assistant), avg responses ~600 tokens, target concurrency 200 concurrent streams, bursts to 5k qps for short windows. Model requested: open-llama-70b quantized or equivalent. They want dedicated A100-ish perf.

rafa: Finance here — 40% is pretty large. Our standard approval matrix: up to 20% at Sales VP, 20–30% needs CRO signoff, >30% requires CFO exec approval + legal signoff on terms. Need ACV estimate and expected lifetime value to justify. What's the projected committed spend after conversion?

mika: Expected committed spend if they convert: ~$540k/year (dedicated plan). POC revenue estimate (6mo at discounted rate) ~45k. They’re sensitive to unit cost because their product margins are thin — POC is to validate latency and reliability.

tanya: Deal Desk — we can structure this as a staged concession: option A) 30% off for 6mo with a signed 12mo conversion clause and milestone (latency validated) OR option B) 40% off for 6mo but with a migration/implementation credit that we classify as one-time professional-services credit (not recurring) and limited to customers signing within 45 days. Option B will still need CFO ok for the 40% list discount component.

alex-sre: On capacity — we can provision a dedicated pool with A100s but need an exact instance count. For the described workload (200 concurrent long sequences), initial config estimate: 4 x A100 (40GB) nodes with autoscale policies for bursts. Latency target <100ms p50 is achievable if we tune batching and KV cache, but need a short perf POC run to verify model variant.

sarah-security: SOC2 is covered via our SOC2 report; we can provide attestation. SSO via SAML/Okta is supported. They asked about data residency — they need EU-only. We have EU region dedicated deploy options but that affects capacity lead time and cost.

jay: If we go forward with a POC, I need to run a perf test. Can we give them a short test script and a temporary token for a sandbox cluster? Example curl for perf harness: 

```

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer TEMP_TOKEN\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{\"model\":\"open-llama-70b-quant\",\"input\":\"<user prompt>\",\"max_tokens\":600}'

```

deploy-bot: sandbox cluster created: sandbox-acmeone-eu, token expires in 7 days.

rafa: Given the numbers, my recommendation: approve up to 30% standard discount now (PMO signoff), and escalate any >30% to CFO. If they're willing to sign the 12mo commit in advance, that reduces risk and might justify 35% with CFO approval.

tanya: I'll draft a one-page approval memo. Required attachments: estimated ARR, POC revenue, proposed credit structure, timeline, and security attestation (soc2 + SSO + data residency). If we go >30% we need CFO sign-off and legal to add a conversion clause (auto-convert pricing terms).

mika: Timeline — customer wants decision by EOD Fri to keep momentum. Can deal desk draft the memo today? I’ll include the ACV and product roadmap note.

tanya: On it. I’ll aim for a draft in 2 hours and ping finance for a quick check. If CFO needs to review, we’ll fast-track an exec summary. :raised_hands:

jay: I’ll drop the perf test payload and sample dataset into the sandbox and share results by tomorrow morning. If perf looks good we can use that as the milestone for conversion.

mika: Thanks all — please tag me if you need any extra customer artifacts (RFP, legal POI). I’ll hold off committing verbally until we have the memo.

tanya: Final note — if we offer 40% for the POC, structure it so the 40% is timeboxed to six months and the migration credit is a separate line item (one-time). That way post-POC invoicing aligns with standard rate card and reduces renewal friction.

mika: Got it. Will wait for the memo.
